question: How many atoms are there in a molecule of water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A molecule of water (H₂O)** consists of **3 atoms**: two hydrogen (H) atoms and one oxygen (O) atom.
 
• **Chemical composition:** Water’s molecular formula, H₂O, clearly indicates that it is made up of **2 hydrogen atoms** and **1 oxygen atom**.
 
• **Covalent bonding:** The hydrogen and oxygen atoms in water are held together by **covalent bonds**, where electrons are shared between the atoms.
 
• **Structural arrangement:** The water molecule has a **bent or V-shaped structure** due to the electron pair repulsion around the oxygen atom, which results in a bond angle of approximately **104.5°**.
 
• **Importance of the composition:** The exact atomic composition and structure of water contribute to its unique properties, such as its polarity, high boiling point, and ability to act as a universal solvent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen atoms in water:**

 
 
• Each hydrogen atom in a water molecule contributes **one electron** to form a covalent bond with the oxygen atom.
 
• Hydrogen is the lightest element and plays a crucial role in forming water’s molecular structure.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen atom in water:**
 
 
• The oxygen atom is more **electronegative** than hydrogen, meaning it pulls the shared electrons closer to itself.
 
• This causes a partial negative charge on oxygen and a partial positive charge on hydrogen, making water a **polar molecule**.
 
 
 
• **Polarity of water:**
 
 
• Due to its bent shape and difference in electronegativity, water is a **polar molecule**.
 
• This polarity allows water to dissolve many substances, making it a **universal solvent**.
 
 
 
• **Unique properties due to structure:**
 
 
• The hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules result in properties like **high surface tension**, **capillary action**, and **high boiling and freezing points**.
 
• These properties are essential for life on Earth and many biological processes.
 
 
 
• **Applications of water’s molecular structure:**
 
 
• Water’s polarity makes it essential for **cellular processes** such as nutrient transport and biochemical reactions.
 
• Its unique structure supports the formation of hydrogen bonds, vital for the structure of **DNA and proteins**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Water as a compound:** Water is a **compound**, not an element, because it consists of more than one type of atom chemically bonded together.
 
• **Molecular weight:** The molecular weight of water is approximately **18 g/mol** (2 hydrogen atoms weighing ~1 g/mol each + 1 oxygen atom weighing ~16 g/mol).
 
• **Water’s role in life:** It is indispensable for life, being a major component of cells, and is involved in essential processes like **photosynthesis** and **cellular respiration**.
 
• **Physical states:** Water exists in all three states of matter—solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapor)—at **Earth’s natural temperature range**.
